name: Debounce Time Calculator
blurb: debounce time for a button type and sampling period
intro: Pick the switch; its worst-case bounce times a safety margin is the window the input must stay stable. At your sampling period that is N equal samples in a row (a counter or an N-bit shift register), which sets the delay a press sees. Bounce figures are typical datasheet maxima and Ganssle's measurements, so a rule of thumb: measure your own switch when it matters.

inputs.label: Sampling period
inputs.help: How often the pin is read (timer tick or scan interval).

inputs.label: Safety margin
inputs.help: Window = worst-case bounce × this. 1.5 … 3 is usual; aged contacts bounce longer.

examples.title: Tact switch scanned from a 1 ms tick

usage: Choose the switch type (or custom and give the worst-case bounce in seconds), the sampling period in seconds, the safety margin as a factor and the supply in volts. It returns the stable-window N (samples in a row), the debounce time N·Ts, the worst-case response from the first contact, the shift-register width that holds N, an RC + Schmitt alternative, and C code. Use it to size a firmware debounce or check an existing scan rate.
sources: J. Ganssle, 'A Guide to Debouncing' (2008): 18 switches measured, mean bounce 1.6 ms, worst 6.2 ms apart from outliers; counter and shift-register debouncers; RC + Schmitt formula R = −t / (C ln(Vth/Vdd))
Switch bounce maxima: Omron B3F tactile switch datasheet (5 ms max), Alps EC11 encoder datasheet (chattering), typical relay and reed switch datasheets; rule of thumb for the other types
Response limit: rule of thumb, under about 50 ms feels instant to a user
